lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.

ch.r: Current assets ÷ current liabilities ≥ 2

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.v: Long-term debt ₹0 cr vs working capital ₹17,305 cr
ch.w: Graham wanted the short-term cushion alone to be able to repay long-term loans.

rd.auditor: Auditor (FY2025-26): opinion unmodified; emphasis of matter: Karnataka Mineral Tax Bill 2024 retrospective levy, ₹15,481.72 crore contingent liability; Recoverability of dues from NMDC Steel Limited, ₹1,851.39 crore plus ₹4,839.36 crore; Recoverability of trade receivables from RINL, ₹4,586.31 crore; KIADB advance of ₹639.61 crore for KVSL land; Common cause compensation demand of ₹1,623.44 crore, sub-judice; Railway Transit Pass penalty of ₹1,620.50 crore, sub-judice; Financial position of Legacy Iron Ore Ltd, foreign subsidiary; key audit matters: 4; contingent liabilities: ₹23,588.47 crore standalone; ₹24,441.86 crore consolidated.

story.what_it_does: NMDC is India's largest iron ore producer, mining a record 53.15 million tonnes in FY26 and selling about 502 lakh tonnes. In FY26 revenue from operations rose 33% to about ₹31,554 crore, with profit after tax of ₹7,421 crore.
story.plans: Management targets 60 million tonnes of production in FY27 and 100 million tonnes of capacity by FY30. Capex was about ₹3,300 crore in FY26 and guidance is about ₹6,000 crore for FY27, with the railway line doubling due October 2026.
story.moat: The notes show scale as its main strength: it is the largest iron ore producer in India. The notes do not describe other advantages, and they flag that big customers JSW and AM-NS have acquired captive mines and may shift away from NMDC ore.

scenarios.story: Production reaches 60 million tonnes in FY27 as Q1's 5.3 million tonnes (vs 4.4 million a year earlier) suggests, and the iron ore EBITDA margin holds near 42%. Capex then builds capacity toward 100 million tonnes by FY30.
signals_to_watch: Production against the 60 million tonne FY27 target
Iron ore EBITDA margin staying near 42%

scenarios.story: Volumes grow, but realisations stay soft (down 13% in Q3 and 5% in Q4 year on year) and the one-time steel trading effect fades. Heavy capex continues while the large receivables take 16 to 24 months to recover.
signals_to_watch: Recovery of receivables from NSL and RINL

scenarios.story: Major customers shift to their own captive mines, and the retrospective Karnataka mineral tax adds a large liability. Delays in railway doubling or clearances could hold growth back beyond 60 million tonnes.
signals_to_watch: Karnataka mineral tax bill (₹15,481.72 crore contingent liability) and presidential assent
Progress on the railway doubling and pending clearances
